rows: Polygons are indicative freehold extents, split by local authority, with unique Land Registry-INSPIRE IDs.
Current publication is 5 July 2026 and files are replaced on the first Sunday monthly.
Catalogue presence does not prove downloaded bytes.
HMLR captures polygon data against British National Grid and warns reprojection can introduce error.
Fresh native file and CRS receipts remain required.
INSPIRE is free under the Open Government Licence with required attribution.
Licence availability does not establish feature identity.
Official DTM 1m metadata identifies EPSG:27700, WCS access and ±15cm RMSE source surveys.
Metadata does not prove current response bytes.
EA documents a persistent WCS endpoint for raw-pixel access.
Each response still requires endpoint, media, size and hash receipts.
Official 2m DTM supports resolution sensitivity checks in EPSG:27700.
It does not replace the pinned 1m primary metric.
Survey resources provide coverage and acquisition context.
Composite pixel lineage must be bound per result.
Terrain 50 is the official coarse terrain product documentation root.
Documentation alone does not validate a package.
Grid supply is 200 by 200 cells, 50m pixels, 10km tiles with ASC/GML/PRJ/AUX/metadata companions.
Exact archive and companion hashes remain required.
OS documents 4m RMSE for Terrain 50 grid data.
This is a coarse screening figure, not parcel confidence.
Product supply includes compressed geographic grid tiles.
One canonical edition per tile must be selected.
Per-tile XML metadata follows GEMINI/INSPIRE conventions.
Metadata must be paired with exact raster bytes.
The API automates discovery and download of OS data packages.
Client trust and response limits remain client responsibilities.
Downloads can be filtered by fileName, format and area; redirect is defined when exactly one match remains.
Final redirect identity and bytes must be validated.
Official products endpoint returns available OpenData products.
Product identity must be unique and pinned.
Official product detail endpoint describes one product ID.
Response contract and final host still require validation.
WCS discovery, description and retrieval are distinct operations tied to offered coverages.
Service, coverage, domain and range must stay bound.
WCS 2.0 defines GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage and GetCoverage behavior.
Requested version and returned service identity require verification.
Coverage descriptions carry domain and range structure including axes, units, data type and nil values.
Global XML token collection is insufficient.
WCS supports explicit interpolation controls through an extension.
Python json defaults allow NaN and Infinity unless allow_nan is false; duplicate object names keep the last value by default.
Strict receipts must reject non-standard and duplicate-key inputs.
subprocess.run supports timeouts and reports return codes; timeout handling concerns the launched child.
Process-tree cleanup needs an explicit platform contract.
Resolved paths and replacement primitives support containment and publication designs.
Durability and symlink policy require additional checks.
